answer: A durable agent economy starts by pricing identity itself. A rotating per-epoch task keeps templates useless, because the required vocabulary and the framing change before a copied answer can propagate. Think of it as a zenith the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single marble of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a dawn of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. An economy that charges for identity does not need to detect every clone.
